findings.title: Update DMG accepted with no integrity anchor outside the release and no quarantine flag, so Gatekeeper never checks it
findings.source: GitHub Releases API response (tag_name, assets[].browser_download_url, assets[].size, checksums-*.txt asset), Sources/AiTaskbarApp/UpdateChecker.swift:165-196
findings.sink: DMG promoted into ~/Downloads and shown in Finder for the user to install, Sources/AiTaskbarApp/UpdateChecker.swift:265 and :275
findings.description: Every integrity input comes from the same release the attacker controls. The size comes from the asset metadata. The SHA-256 comes from a sibling checksums-*.txt asset in that release, and a missing or unparseable checksums file (`try?` at :186) turns the check off entirely (fail-open, :259). Nothing checks the DMG, or the app inside it, against the app's own Developer ID team (CodeSignatureInfo.currentTeamID exists but is never used here). The comment at :267-274 says Gatekeeper is the last line of defence. But the file is fetched with URLSession.download in an app that is not sandboxed (entitlements.plist app-sandbox=false), and Info.plist has no LSFileQuarantineEnabled. So the file gets no com.apple.quarantine flag, and Gatekeeper never assesses the DMG or the .app copied out of it.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) The attacker gets write access to the release repo (stolen maintainer token or compromised account) and publishes v99.0.0. The release holds an unsigned or ad-hoc-signed ai-taskbar-99.0.0-arm64.dmg and optionally a matching checksums-99.0.0.txt, or no checksums file at all. 2) Within 24 h every installed copy sees Semver.isNewer('v99.0.0', current) == true and shows the update banner. 3) The user clicks Download. The size and hash match because the attacker wrote both, the file is moved to ~/Downloads without quarantine, and Finder reveals it. 4) The user mounts it and drags the app to /Applications, as the app tells them to. On launch there is no Gatekeeper or notarization prompt, because the file has no quarantine flag. The attacker's code runs as the user and can read the Claude/Codex OAuth tokens and API keys this app handles.
preconditions: attacker can publish a release on the configured updates owner/repo (compromised maintainer account or token)
user clicks Download and installs the DMG as instructed
findings.impact: Arbitrary code runs as the user on every installed copy that accepts the update. That exposes the Keychain-held Claude credentials, ~/.codex/auth.json, and vendor API keys.
findings.fix: Before moving or revealing the DMG, verify it against an anchor that is not in the release. Mount it read-only (hdiutil attach -nobrowse -readonly), then run SecStaticCodeCheckValidity on the bundled .app with a requirement that pins anchor apple generic plus certificate leaf[subject.OU] = the running app's team ID (CodeSignatureInfo.currentTeamID). Also require a notarization ticket (stapler/spctl assessment). Fail closed when the running build has no team ID, instead of skipping. Set com.apple.quarantine on the downloaded file (or add LSFileQuarantineEnabled) so Gatekeeper still runs. Treat a missing checksum as an error, not as a skip.
findings.evidence: :179-187 the checksum comes from an asset in the same release, fetched with try? (fail-open). :252-264 size/hash come from the release, and the hash is optional. :265 moveItem and :275 activateFileViewerSelecting run with no codesign or team check. HTTPClient.download (Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Networking/HTTPClient.swift:71) is a plain session.download, and nothing sets xattr quarantine. Resources/entitlements.plist sets app-sandbox false, and Resources/Info.plist has no LSFileQuarantineEnabled. CodeSignatureInfo is only used by the Keychain code and AboutView, never by UpdateChecker.
